newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Rank profits to be hit by charges.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Rank profits to be hit by charges.

text.p: British diversified company Rank Group Plc is expected to report sharply lower annual profits next Thursday after around 185 million pounds of restructuring charges and poperty write-offs.

Some analysts, who cut profit forecasts after a disappointing trading statement in December sent Rank's stock diving six percent, are expecting pretax profits of around 100 million pounds after exceptional charges.
Normalised pretax profits are expected at 283-330 million stg, compared with 658 million pounds last year. Analysts have pencilled in a 14-17p dividend, up from 11p last time.
Over the last 12 months, Rank's shares have underperformed the FTSE All Share index by about 23 percent -- and the leisure sector by a hefty 27 percent, according to Reuters Security 3000 graphics.
"I think what the market is looking for is proof that the business is being better run. But that seems to be somewhat slow coming, which is why the shares have underperformed," said one analyst.
Rank on Friday completed its senior management team under chief executive Andrew Teare by appointing Jerry Fowden managing director of its holidays division.
The business, including the holiday villages Butlin's and Oasis, due to open in the Lake district in May, has turned in a dull performance. Teare says he is determined to turn it around.

Rank is expected to sell its stake soon in office equipment joint venture with America's Xerox Corp, Rank Xerox. But it has declined to comment on talk that it also plans the imminent sale of its film distribution business.
Rank's shares, which have swung from a high of 549p to a low of 396p this year, were trading at 412p on Friday, a loss of 5.5 pence.
